_readme: Rerolls (6 Nov, Matt: "these need re rolling"): six first-person guns that came out side-on, doubled or wrong. Seeds +1000; no style_image (the side-on icon pulled each into profile) - the weapon described in words, big_revolver.png kept as the view's reference. 6 jobs x $0.08.

jobs.description: First-person view of the player's own two hands in fingerless wool gloves holding a single olive-drab military rifle with a short telescopic sight on top and a stubby grenade-launcher tube under its barrel, shouldered, one hand at the pistol grip and one under the launcher, coming in from the bottom right corner of the frame, as in a light-gun arcade game; the sleeves of a worn work jacket at the wrists. The weapon sits low in the frame: its body and stock run down and back into the bottom right corner, tucked into the shoulder and mostly cut off by the frame's edge, never rising above the barrel; the top of the weapon stays below the middle of the frame. Seen from behind and just above the weapon, looking straight down the barrel, strongly foreshortened: the muzzle points away into the scene towards the middle of the frame and the back of the weapon comes towards the viewer at the bottom right; not a side view, not in profile. The same viewpoint, framing and grip as the reference image of the revolver. One weapon only, held by exactly two hands. Only the hands and what they hold, coming in from the bottom right edge. Realistic painted pixel art, soft overcast light, muted cool northern palette, worn and lived-in, post-collapse Britain on a grey day; no black outlines, not anime, not a cartoon, not glossy; no text, no logos.
jobs._where: your hands: Regimental rifle (primary; falls back to hands_rifle) - reroll 6 Nov: two rifles overlapping: the launcher drawn as a second gun beside a scoped one, and side-on
